cover.headline: One card deal paid Delta {more than its operating profit.}
cover.credit: Photo: Oleg Yunakov / CC0 via Wikimedia Commons

slides.label: THE SETUP
slides.headline: Every swipe on a {Delta Amex card} pays Delta.
slides.body: American Express is the exclusive issuer of Delta SkyMiles cards. Cardholders earn miles on their spending, and *Amex pays Delta* for it. The partnership goes back to *1996* and now runs through *2029.*
slides.source: Delta; American Express; The Points Guy

slides.label: THE NUMBER
slides.headline: $8.2 billion in {2025.}
slides.body: That's Delta's *American Express remuneration* in 2025, up 11% in a year. Delta's entire *operating income* was $5.8 billion. ==Revenue isn't profit.== But this one payment was bigger than the airline's whole operating income.

slides.label: THE GROWTH
rows: *1 million+ new cards* for the fourth straight year.
Delta targets *$10 billion* a year within a few years.
slides.source: Delta FY2025 results; The Points Guy

slides.label: THE PIVOT
slides.headline: So Delta sells {more than seats.}
slides.body: Premium cabins and other non-ticket revenue, loyalty included, made up *60%* of Delta's adjusted revenue in 2025, up from 57% the year before.

last.headline: The plane gets you there. {The card gets paid.}
last.body: When everyday spending is what you sell, the airline becomes the billboard.
